output.answer_markdown: IFF states that operating cash flow is the primary source of funds for capital investment needs, dividends paid to shareholders and debt service repayments [1], and it anticipates that cash flows from operations and availability under existing credit facilities will be sufficient to meet its investing and financing needs [2]. Following the Merger with N&B, IFF assumed the indebtedness N&B incurred in its debt financings, including the term loan facilities and a series of Senior Notes totaling $6.250 billion [3]. The N&B term loan was a senior unsecured term loan credit facility of $1.250 billion [4].

provenance.quote: Operating cash flow provides the primary source of funds for capital investment needs, dividends paid to shareholders and debt service repayments.

claims.text: Operating cash flow is the primary source of funds for capital investment needs, dividends paid to shareholders and debt service repayments.

provenance.quote: We anticipate that cash flows from operations and availability under our existing credit facilities will be sufficient to meet our investing and financing needs.

provenance.quote: Following the Merger, we assumed the indebtedness incurred by N&B in the debt financings, which included (i) the 2024 Term Loan Facility and 2026 Term Loan Facility and (ii) a series of Senior Notes in the aggregate amount of $6.250 billion with maturities ranging from 2 to 30 years.

claims.text: Following the Merger, IFF assumed the indebtedness N&B incurred, including a series of Senior Notes in the aggregate amount of $6.250 billion.
